messages:
jin: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a decision on the runtime policy format. Do we go DSL (compact, expressive) or strict JSON AST (easier validation, less magic)?

sara: leaning JSON AST. Easier to validate and to UI-ify for customers.

mike: concern: JSON configs become verbose for complex fallthroughs. DSL lets ops write rules faster.

oliver: tradeoff: DSL -> harder to debug and test, but smaller payloads. JSON -> easier to compile to decision tree and to cache.

reena: major operational requirement: per-tenant overrides + quick emergency bypass (operator-initiated). That pushes me to a composable AST so we can diff/merge.

jin: agree. Also we need evaluation cost accounting — policies should expose estimated "eval_cost" so router can decide budget-aware routing.

mike: what about hybrid? Customer-facing UI takes a guided DSL, server compiles to canonical JSON AST that runtime consumes.

sara: +1 to hybrid. We can store canonical AST in S3/DB and show source DSL in UI/editor. That aids rollback and linting.

oliver: runtime behaviors to decide: short-circuit order (first-match vs score-based), attribute weighting (latency vs cost vs region), and caching of rule outputs per request key.

jin: proposal: compile to a DAG of match + score nodes. Nodes annotated with anchors: {priority, expected_cost, ttl_ms}.

reena: sample canonical AST snippet:
```
{"type":"match","expr":{"and":[{"eq":["region","eu-west-1"]},{"lte":["latency_ms",200]}]},"on_match":{"action":"route","target":"dedicated-eu"},"meta":{"priority":10,"expected_cost":0.02}}
```

mike: nice. runtime can evaluate cheaper predicates first. Also we should support probabilistic routing for canaries, e.g., `probability:0.03`.

sara: observability: every evaluation should emit a compact trace id + chosen rule id. Need sampling for high QPS.

jin: enforcement: policies must be sandboxed. No arbitrary code execution. Also we need a safe subset for arithmetic and string ops.

oliver: caching: cache rule results by prefix of user/request attributes. TTL default 5s, configurable per rule. Beware stale routing when rolling out model variants.

reena: per-tenant rate/budget limits: if cost burn exceeds budget, policy engine should downgrade to cheap-model fallback and emit alert.

mike: testing harness: produce randomized request generator + property tests to ensure determinism and no rule ambiguity. Also policy linter for unreachable rules.

sara: UX note: show ranked list of matched rules and why earlier ones lost (cost/priority). That makes debugging much easier.

policy-bot: Deploy note: test-runner job #482 queued for policy-compiler branch. @jin @sara

jin: ok next steps: draft hybrid RFC for compiler contract (DSL -> AST), define canonical AST schema, add metadata fields (priority, expected_cost, ttl_ms, id). I'll put a PR up with examples.

sara: I can prototype the UI diff view.

oliver: I'll spike a runtime evaluator that consumes AST + emits traces.

reena: I'll write the linter rules and budget enforcement simulation.

mike: roll call for design review Weds 10am.

jin: thanks all. filing notes here so GH RFC can reference this thread. :thumbsup:
